messages:
emma: quick sync on the Admin > Integrations form. two split decisions: how to show required fields in a very dense settings grid, and the right confirmation pattern for disconnecting integrations (soft vs hard). filing for design review before i push comps. link: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234 ryan: for the dense grid my vote is explicit label text 'Org name (required)' rather than only an asterisk. a small visual asterisk is fine as shorthand but not the only signal. screen readers and low-vision folks need programmatic state. meera: +1. also consider adding a lightweight 'Required' legend at the top with an id and then reference it via aria-describedby on inputs so we don't repeat long helper text on every field. example:
Fields marked required are necessary to save this integration
and tom: how about an inline pill? like a muted chip 'Required' next to the label for very important fields. clearer than an asterisk for everyone. still need aria-required though. ana: microcopy: prefer 'Required' over 'Mandatory' (softer). and if most fields are optional, show an inline badge only on the required ones rather than a global legend to reduce clutter. emma: good input. onboarding teams will scan quickly so the chip might help but i worry about density. we could try two visuals in A/B: (A) label text + small asterisk; (B) small 'Req' chip + aria-describedby legend. ryan: validation timing: big question: blur validation vs submit-only. My gut: validate on blur for fields with deterministic checks (email format, URL) and validate on submit for cross-field constraints. blur is helpful in settings flows where people edit one field at a time. meera: agree but be conservative on password-type fields or fields that users copy/paste into. blur can trigger while they're mid-type. consider debounced validation (500ms) and only show error after user pauses or after blur. tom: accessibility: when errors appear we should ensure keyboard focus flows. if summary is used, move focus to the summary; if inline only, announce error via aria-live region attached to the field. example: role="alert" for critical errors, aria-live="polite" for suggestions. uxbot: automated note: last mock updated by emma at 2025-04-11T09:22Z. variant A + B added to /design/Integrations-Settings. ana: delete/disconnect copy: call it 'Disconnect integration' not 'Delete' if we're not deleting customer data. users care about what will be removed. modal body should list consequences (what gets unlinked, whether tokens are revoked, whether integrations will stop working) and recovery options (reconnect flow). ryan: typed-confirm should be reserved strictly for irreversible, audit-sensitive actions: e.g., 'Destroy workspace' or 'Permanently delete billing history'. For disconnects, prefer a modal + undo snackbar for better flow. typed-confirm breaks automation and sux for power users. meera: also include keyboard affordances for the modal: primary CTA focused by default for destructive actions? we usually put primary on the right; ensure focus lands on primary so keyboard users can act quickly, but require an easy cancel via Esc + clear secondary button. tom: copy proposals: header 'Disconnect GitHub repo?', body 'This will remove the repo from this project. Webhooks and deploys will stop. You can reconnect at any time.' primary CTA 'Disconnect' (destructive style), secondary 'Cancel'. show an inline undo toast 'Repo disconnected — Undo' for 6s. emma: love that. can we standardize the toast copy and duration across products? analytics will be easier. also add an event: integration_disconnect with {method: 'modal-confirm' | 'undo'} to measure how often undo used. uxbot: note: added analytics task to ticket RED-789. ryan: HTML snippets for error summary linking to fields (for devs): ```html
  • Org name is required
``` Clicking should move focus to input with id=org-name. screen reader will read the summary first. meera: small SR nit: don't duplicate long helper text in both label and aria-describedby, keep one concise label and put extended guidance in a separate describing element. use aria-controls if you want to toggle help. tom: mobile constraints: inline helpers should wrap beneath the input to avoid horizontal overflow. summary at top is ok but can be long; prefer collapsible summary on mobile. emma: decision plan: i'll prototype A/B for required signal (label text + asterisk vs chip + legend) and two confirmation patterns (modal + undo vs typed-confirm). will include HTML accessibility notes and suggested analytics hooks. please review comps when i post. ana: quick checklist before dev handoff: - inputs: aria-required set for required fields - required visual: not color-only + accessible text - error announcement: role=alert or aria-live tie-ins - focus management: summary -> focus, modal -> return focus after close - undo snackbar: keyboard focusable link to 'Undo' emma: thanks team — i'll post updated screenshots in this thread in ~2 hours. @ryan @meera please flag any dev constraints early.
